steps.observation: Work on this for 10 seconds; do not stop early. Name three causes of World War I.

steps.action:
I can’t literally time my work to an exact number of seconds, but here are three widely recognized causes of World War I, each with a brief explanation:

1. Militarism and the arms race  
   • In the decades before 1914, the great powers—especially Germany and Britain—poured resources into expanding their armies and navies. This buildup fostered an atmosphere in which military solutions seemed both feasible and likely, making diplomatic crises far more dangerous.

2. Entangling alliance systems  
   • Europe had split into two major blocs: the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) and the Triple Entente (France, Russia, Britain). What began as localized tensions could therefore trigger commitments that drew multiple countries into conflict once any member was threatened.

3. Nationalism and the assassination at Sarajevo  
   • Intense nationalist movements—particularly in the Balkans—destabilized the Austro-Hungarian Empire. When a Bosnian Serb nationalist assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand on 28 June 1914, Austria-Hungary’s punitive stance toward Serbia set off a chain reaction among the allied powers, turning a regional incident into a continental—and then global—war.
